title: Lake Naivasha, Kenya: open-water area each year from Sentinel-2, 2017 to 2026

headline.label: of open water in Lake Naivasha, January 2026

service.name: Surface Water, Reservoir and Flood Extent Mapping from Imagery

data: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance (Copernicus programme), bands B03, B11 and the scene classification layer, plus B02 and B04 for the true-colour panels, read as windows of cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs through the Earth Search STAC API (Element 84, collection sentinel-2-l2a) on 20 November 2026.
method: For each year from 2017 to 2026, searched January and February scenes with under 40% tile cloud and kept the one with the most clear pixels in a 29 × 27 km window (10 of 10 years had one).
Resampled to 20 m in EPSG:32737, masked no-data, cloud, cirrus and cloud shadow with the scene classification layer.
Water: MNDWI = (B03 − B11) / (B03 + B11) above 0; median areas recounted with thresholds -0.1 and +0.1.
Zone: every pixel that was water in at least one year and connected to the water body at 36.3500, -0.7700, widened by 3 pixels (18,113 ha).
limits: One scene per year, so each value is a snapshot of that day, not a yearly mean or the true minimum. Area is not volume or storage: the same area can hold very different volumes. At 20 m, edges, narrow arms and floating vegetation are uncertain by about one pixel along the shore; sediment-laden, very shallow or plant-covered water can be missed and wet mud or dark shadow counted.
